questions.q: What happens when you listen to someone before offering solutions?
a: They get space to sort through their feelings and calm down
They quickly forget what originally upset them
They expect you to solve the problem for them
They become more defensive about their position
questions.why: Lesson 1 says listening first lets people think things through and dispute irrational feelings.

questions.q: In the negotiation story, what did the officer do that worked?
a: He named the man's feeling that this seemed the only way out
He listed every legal option available to the man
He promised the man would not face any charges
He called the man's family to come to the scene
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the officer listened to the man's feelings until he calmed down.

questions.q: Which three layers of thinking does the summary describe?
a: Reptilian instinct, mammalian emotion and rational analysis
Conscious, subconscious and unconscious thought
Sensory, memory and imagination processes
Logical, creative and social intelligence
questions.why: Lesson 2 outlines the instinctual, emotional and rational layers of the brain.

questions.q: Why should you address someone's feelings before making your point?
a: They can then listen using the rational part of their brain
They will owe you a favor afterward
It proves that you are the real expert
It shortens the conversation considerably
questions.why: Lesson 2 says people who feel understood can then listen rationally.

questions.q: What does the summary mean by baring your neck?
a: Show vulnerability so others can connect and want to help
Admit fault even when you did nothing wrong
Raise your voice to show confidence and strength
Step back and let other people argue it out
questions.why: Lesson 3 says vulnerability invites connection and makes people more willing to listen.
